questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The __collision__ was witnessed by the pedestrians.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "violent accident".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, **"The collision was witnessed by the pedestrians," **the underlined segment refers to **"collision". **

 
 
• **​**This term indicates some **sort of accident or impact **where two or more objects hit each other.
 
 
 
• **When looking at the four options:**
 
 
• **"powerful blast" **pertains to an explosion, and does not necessarily equate to a **“collision” **where two objects come into contact with force.
 
• **"funeral procession" **is a ceremony commemorating the deceased, which does not fit the concept of a collision.
 
• **"violent accident" **might involve a collision and can appropriately replace **"collision" **in the sentence whilst preserving the original meaning.
 
• **"protest march" **refers to a public act of protesting, which does not imply a collision.
 
 
 
• Therefore, based on this analysis, the most suitable substitute for the underlined segment **"collision" **in the given sentence is: **"violent accident".**
 
• So the sentence reads: **"The violent accident was witnessed by the pedestrians."**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3".**

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in past tense form.**

Aksa Thomas comes to attend the session so early.

options.text: Aksa Thomas came to attend the session so early.
Aksa Thomas has come to attend the session so early.
Aksa Thomas may come to attend the session so early.
Aksa Thomas will come to attend the session so early.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Aksa Thomas came to attend the session so early."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The **‘past tense’** form of a verb, as the term suggests, can be used to speak about or represent an event or action that already happened in the past. 
 
• **Structure: Subject + V2 + Object**
 
 
• **Example**: *She invited me.*
 
 
 
• To convert the sentence **"Aksa Thomas comes to attend the session so early" **into the past tense, we must follow these steps:
 
 
• Change the present tense verb** "comes"** to its past tense form, which is** "came."**
 
• Keep the rest of the sentence structure unchanged.
 
 
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

 

Correct sentence: *Aksa Thomas came to attend the session so early.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

APJ Abdul Kalam was born in a middle class family. He was a short boy ________ ordinary looks.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'with rather'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct preposition to use after "**boy**" is "**with**" as it is often used to indicate a particular feature or quality that someone or something has.
 
• The word '**rather**' is used to make a statement or opinion stronger, especially one that is critical. It is appropriately fitting in this context as it suggests that APJ Abdul Kalam's looks were not extraordinary or noticeable, but ordinary.
 
• Option 1 ‘**with either**’ and Option 4 ‘**neither**’ are not grammatically correct and don’t make sense in the given context.
 
• Option 2 ‘**with as**’ is ungrammatical in this context; '**as**' is generally used for making comparisons, not describing attributes, which is the case in this sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is:** Option 3.**

**Correct Sentence:* ****APJ Abdul Kalam was born in a middle class family. He was a short boy **with rather** ordinary looks.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• APJ Abdul Kalam, also known as the '**Missile Man of India**,' rose from humble beginnings to become the President of India and a globally respected scientist, proving that ordinary looks have no bearing on extraordinary achievements.
 
• '**Rather**' is a flexible word in English and can be used for emphasis, as in this context, or could mean '**to a certain extent**' or '**somewhat**.'
